summary: An unnamed first-person narrator, injured from earlier events involving napalm, gunfire and a staged car crash, leaps a roughly thirteen-foot gap from one rooftop to a neighboring building that has been destroyed by a demolition blast. After landing, the narrator picks through the rubble of the third floor, finds a ladder-like staircase into the second floor, and cautiously descends, wary of rigged explosives. The second floor turns out to be a gang's barracks with stacked bunks, a rusted kitchen and boxed MREs. The passage is a fiction excerpt from 'Book 6 — part 48'.
one_line: A wounded narrator leaps across a gap to a blast-ruined building and cautiously explores a gang's barracks on its second floor.
key_facts: The vertical distance between the two roofs was barely over thirteen feet.
The narrator had fallen farther plenty of times before making the leap.
The narrator tossed bits of roof over the landing area to check whether anything was still live.
The narrator ran at the roof edge with only purple-blue sky visible ahead.
The narrator's jump is described as a perfect parabola with an instant of weightlessness at the top.
The narrator lands exactly where aimed and rolls out, then sits for a minute.
The narrator's ribs twinge and a cough follows, linked to earlier napalm, being shot, and an intentional car crash.
The third floor of the other building is a rubble-strewn forest of debris and wall nubs.
Debris includes loose papers under concrete blocks, a broken computer monitor, and a dismembered office chair.
The narrator fears explosives that did not go off in the original blast and wonders whether the second floor was rigged beyond the perimeter.
The narrator reaches the bottom of a ladder-like staircase, now a skylight, without triggering an explosion.
The second floor was set up like a barracks with bunks stacked in rooms with no privacy.
A rusted-out kitchen on the second floor holds boxed MREs.
The narrator doubts the kitchen plumbing is working.
